text: Parfit uses the fission case (each brain hemisphere transplanted into a different body, each successor fully psychologically continuous with the original) chiefly to argue for which conclusion?
choices: That the survivor is determinately whichever person receives the left hemisphere
That each of us is fundamentally a biological organism, so fission cannot really occur
That identity is not what matters in survival; what matters is Relation R, which can hold without numerical identity
That personal identity is constituted by the narrative unity of a life
explanation: Because both successors are equally continuous with the original, none can be singled out as the strictly identical one, yet the person clearly survives in the way we care about — so Parfit concludes that what matters is Relation R (psychological continuity and connectedness with the right cause), not identity. Choosing the left-hemisphere recipient is the arbitrary answer he rejects; animalism treats fission as impossible rather than as revealing Relation R; and narrative identity is a different tradition.
